---
title: "CAS PCPA Practice Project"
subtitle: "Variable Selection"
---

## Overview

In this video we perform variable selection starting from the baseline
model fit. We use drop1 with the Chi-square test to
iteratively remove non-significant variables, then check VIF on the
resulting model to identify any remaining multicollinearity concerns.
The iterative nature of this process reflects how variable selection
is done in practice - each removal is a documented, justified decision.

---

1. Load Libraries

Load tidyverse, statmod, car, and tweedie for modeling and diagnostics
```{r}
# install.packages("tidyverse")
# install.packages("statmod")
# install.packages("car")
# install.packages("tweedie")
library(tidyverse)
library(statmod)
library(car)
library(tweedie)
```

---

2. Load the Data and Baseline Model

Read the training set with factors already applied, Tweedie p, and
baseline model into R
```{r}
train   <- read_csv("train_modela.csv")
p       <- readRDS("tweedie_p.rds")
model_A <- readRDS("model_A.rds")

cat("Using Tweedie p:", round(p, 4), "\n")
cat("Baseline AIC:", round(AICtweedie(model_A), 2), "\n")
```

---

3. Re-apply Factor Levels

Factor levels are not preserved when saving to CSV so we need to
re-apply them after loading
```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    gender            = factor(gender),
    marital_status    = factor(marital_status),
    coverage_type     = factor(coverage_type),
    deductible        = factor(deductible),
    make              = factor(make),
    body_type         = factor(body_type),
    vehicle_use       = factor(vehicle_use),
    num_cylinders     = factor(num_cylinders),
    anti_theft_device = factor(anti_theft_device),
    safety_rating     = factor(safety_rating),
    region            = factor(region),
    urban_rural       = factor(urban_rural),
    tort_environment  = factor(tort_environment),
    catastrophe_risk  = factor(catastrophe_risk)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    gender            = relevel(gender, ref = "F"),
    marital_status    = relevel(marital_status, ref = "Married"),
    coverage_type     = relevel(coverage_type, ref = "Liability Only"),
    deductible        = relevel(deductible, ref = "500"),
    make              = relevel(make, ref = "Toyota"),
    body_type         = relevel(body_type, ref = "Sedan"),
    vehicle_use       = relevel(vehicle_use, ref = "Pleasure"),
    safety_rating     = relevel(safety_rating, ref = "3"),
    urban_rural       = relevel(urban_rural, ref = "Suburban"),
    tort_environment  = relevel(tort_environment, ref = "Moderate"),
    catastrophe_risk  = relevel(catastrophe_risk, ref = "Medium")
  )
```

---

4. Initial drop1

Run drop1 on the baseline model to assess the contribution of each
variable. Variables with high p-values are candidates for removal.
We remove the least significant variable first and repeat.
```{r}
drop1(model_A, test = "Chisq")
```

---

5. Iterative Variable Removal

Remove the least significant variable identified by drop1 and refit.
Update the variable name based on your drop1 output each time and
repeat until all remaining variables have p-values below 0.05.

Round 0 - remove 'make' due to VIF
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_A, . ~ . - make)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 1 - remove the least significant variable
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - anti_theft_device)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 2 - remove the next least significant variable if applicable
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - num_cylinders)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 3 - continue until all remaining variables are significant
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - marital_status)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 4
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - body_type)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 5
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - deductible)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 6
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - safety_rating)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 7
```{r}
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - age)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

Round 7
```{r}
model_B <- model_current
model_current <- update(model_current, . ~ . - vehicle_use)
drop1(model_current, test = "Chisq")
```

---

6. Review Model After Variable Selection

Print the summary of the model after variable selection
```{r}
summary(model_current)
model_C <- model_current
```

Review fit statistics comparing baseline to selected model
```{r}
cat("Baseline AIC:        ", round(AICtweedie(model_A), 2), "\n")
cat("Model B AIC:  ", round(AICtweedie(model_B), 2), "\n")
cat("Model C AIC:  ", round(AICtweedie(model_C), 2), "\n")
cat("% Deviance Explained:", round((1 - model_current$deviance / model_current$null.deviance) * 100, 2), "%\n")
```

---

7. Check VIF on Selected Model

Check VIF on the model after variable selection to identify any
remaining multicollinearity concerns
```{r}
vif_results <- vif(model_C)
round(vif_results, 3)
```

---

8. Final Review of Selected Model

Print the final model summary after all variable selection decisions
```{r}
summary(model_C)
```

Review final fit statistics
```{r}
cat("Baseline AIC:             ", round(AICtweedie(model_A), 2), "\n")
cat("Model C AIC: ", round(AICtweedie(model_C), 2), "\n")
cat("% Deviance Explained:     ", round((1 - model_current$deviance / model_current$null.deviance) * 100, 2), "%\n")
```

---

10. Save the Selected Model

Save the selected model for use in subsequent scripts
```{r}
saveRDS(model_C, "model_C.rds")
cat("Selected model saved to model_C.rds\n")
```

---

## Key Observations

- Variable selection was performed using drop1 with the Chi-square test starting from the baseline model fit in Video 15
- Variables were removed one at a time in order of least significance until all remaining variables had p-values below 0.05
- VIF was checked after variable selection to identify any remaining multicollinearity concerns
- If make had a high VIF and showed weak signal in the mean pure premium analysis it was dropped as a deliberate documented decision
- The iterative drop1 process reflects how variable selection is done in practice and demonstrates the kind of systematic judgment the PCPA project expects
- The selected model is carried forward into Video 17 where we perform feature engineering on surviving variables
